subject: gk
question: ________ empowers the President to remove inconsistencies between laws passed by the Parliament and State Legislatures and the subjects included in the concurrent list.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 254**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 254 of the Indian Constitution deals with inconsistencies between laws made by the Parliament and laws made by the State Legislatures.
 
• It empowers the President to remove any inconsistency that may arise between laws passed by the Parliament and those passed by State Legislatures on subjects included in the Concurrent List.
 
• If there is a conflict between the central and state laws on a subject in the Concurrent List, the central law prevails over the state law.
 
• The President can give his/her assent to a state law that is inconsistent with a central law, after which the state law will prevail in that state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concurrent List:**

 
 
• The Concurrent List is one of the three lists in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution that outlines the subjects on which both the Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate.
 
• Some examples of subjects in the Concurrent List include criminal law, criminal procedure, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy and insolvency, and trusts and trustees.
 
 
 
• **Article 254(2):**
 
 
• Article 254(2) specifically allows a state law that is inconsistent with a central law to prevail in that state if it receives the President's assent.
 
• This provision ensures that the central government can maintain uniformity on certain subjects while still allowing states to enact laws that cater to their specific needs.
 
 
 
• **Seventh Schedule:**
 
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains three lists: the Union List, the State List, and the Concurrent List.
 
• The Union List includes subjects on which only the Parliament can legislate, the State List includes subjects on which only the State Legislatures can legislate, and the Concurrent List includes subjects on which both can legislate.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Powers:**
 
 
• The distribution of legislative powers between the Parliament and State Legislatures is one of the key features of the Indian federal system.
 
• This distribution is intended to ensure that both levels of government can operate effectively within their respective domains.
